I've been working this land for 40 years. I know every corner of Quzhou — the soils, how the groundwater has been dropping year after year, and what the markets have been doing. At 70, I'm not chasing experiments. I manage what I know.

**My thinking:**

My 7.7 mu is split between the wheat-maize double-crop rotation on 5 mu, and 2.7 mu of cotton on a separate plot. The wheat and maize occupy the same ground — wheat goes in October, comes out in June, maize goes straight back in.

**Wheat (5 mu, winter):** I'll use an improved variety, something like Jimai or Kenong — proven in this county. I don't overwater. The water table under Quzhou has been falling my whole farming life. I irrigate at sowing, again at jointing, and once more at heading if the spring is dry. Three times total. I apply nitrogen in two splits — base dose at sowing, then topdress at jointing. I spray twice: once at the seedling stage for disease protection, once around heading for aphids and rust. Rotary tillage after maize harvest in autumn to turn in the stubble.

**Maize (5 mu, summer):** I plant hybrid seed — I've used Zhengdan 958 and Xianyu 335 over the years, I'll stick with something similar. I direct seed into the wheat stubble without tilling. Nitrogen goes in at two points: some at planting, the rest when the plant is knee-high. Two irrigations unless it rains well — summer usually brings some moisture. Two pesticide passes: one early for stem borer, one later if needed.

**Cotton (2.7 mu, spring-autumn):** Cotton still pays better per mu than grain if I manage it properly. I use a Bt hybrid — cuts down pest pressure considerably compared to what we dealt with 20 years ago. I plough this plot in spring before planting. Cotton is thirsty and needs more care — four irrigations through the season, five pesticide applications (aphids, spider mites, bollworm still show up even with Bt). I put more potassium here because cotton strips it from the soil.
